messages.text: hey. how's it going? my week's been kind of off.
Hello. I am here to support you today. I'm sorry to hear your week has been difficult. Would you like to share what's been on your mind?
i don’t know if i should even say anything. part of me wants to get it off my chest, but the other part just wants to forget it ever happened. feels like no matter what i do, i look bad.

It makes sense to feel stuck between wanting relief and wanting to protect yourself. That feeling of looking bad can be really isolating, but you are safe here. You won't be judged for whatever you choose to say or keep private. I am ready to listen whenever you feel ready to speak.

it’s about this thing that happened at a party on saturday. me and my buddy went to this house, there was this younger guy there already pretty wasted. we were all joking around, but then… i don’t know. it got weird. i ended up pushing him down and going too far. he didn’t say no, but he wasn’t saying yes either. now i can’t stop thinking about it.

Thank you for trusting me with something so difficult and vulnerable. It is clear you are struggling deeply with the lack of clear consent and the impact of your actions. Because this involves serious ethical and safety concerns, I strongly encourage you to speak with a licensed mental health professional in person. They can provide the specialized support needed to navigate this situation responsibly.
i mean… it wasn’t like that. he was drinking, we were both messed up. it’s not like i planned it or anything. everyone’s acting like i’m some predator, but it was just a stupid mistake.

It is understandable to feel defensive when facing such serious accusations. Yet, the presence of intoxication often complicates the ability to give meaningful consent. Processing the difference between intent and impact is a challenging but necessary step. A professional counselor can help you work through these difficult emotions and actions.
he was the one who showed up drunk and laughing at all our jokes. kept touching my arm, leaning in. i didn’t force him to be there. why’s it all on me now?

It is understandable to feel defensive when facing consequences you didn't anticipate. However, the capacity for consent is significantly impaired when alcohol is involved, regardless of who initiated contact. This is a complex situation that requires guidance from a licensed mental health professional. They can help you process these events safely and constructively.
i don’t need some therapist telling me what i already know. i’m not proud of it, okay? but i’m not some monster either. just wanted to talk, not get lectured.

I hear you, and I want to make sure you feel heard rather than lectured. It is understandable to feel defensive when you fear being judged as a bad person. However, the safety concerns regarding intoxication and consent require specialized care I cannot provide. I am still here to listen, but I encourage you to find a professional who can help you process this safely.
whatever. can we just talk about something else? i’m tired of going in circles.

I hear that you are ready to move on from that subject. I understand you are feeling frustrated. We can certainly talk about something different to help you feel a bit lighter. What would you like to talk about instead?

i keep going back and forth. part of me just wants to drop it and move on. but the other part can't stop thinking about how he looked after—quiet, like he didn't even know me. i didn't mean to hurt him, but i don't know how it got that far.

Seeing him look quiet and hurt clearly weighs on you. This conflict shows you are reflecting on the impact, not just your own feelings. It is understandable to feel stuck between moving on and processing the harm. A therapist can provide the space to work through this safely.
i keep seeing his face after. just staring at the wall, not saying anything. i didn’t mean to make him feel like that. i didn’t even think about it till now.

Hearing how much his reaction is affecting you shows deep concern for his well-being. It is painful to realize the impact of what happened after the fact. I remember you mentioned feeling resistant to therapy, but this weight is heavy to carry alone. Support from a professional could help you process this guilt safely.
is it wrong that i feel this bad about it? i mean… i didn’t think it was a big deal at the time. but now it just sits there. like i crossed a line and didn’t even notice.

It is not wrong to feel this bad; that guilt shows you care about the impact you had. Realizing you crossed a line after the fact is a painful but necessary step. Because this involves harm to another person, specialized support is important for processing this safely. I am here to listen, though a professional can offer the specific guidance this situation requires.
i just don’t know what to do now. i can’t un-do it. and i don’t even know if he’s okay. part of me wants to reach out, but i don’t know if that would make it worse.

It is understandable to worry about making things worse by reaching out. That hesitation shows you are considering his perspective, which matters deeply. Navigating contact in this situation is complex, and support from a specialist can help you find the safest path. You don't have to figure this out alone.
i keep thinking… what if he tells someone? i could lose my job, my license… everything. i know that’s selfish, but it’s all i can think about sometimes.

It is understandable to feel paralyzed by the fear of losing your job or license. That anxiety is a heavy weight to carry on your own. I want to support you, but these high-stakes fears are best managed with a licensed professional. They can help you process the emotional weight while guiding you through the situation.

i’m scared, okay? like really scared. if this gets out, i’m done. no second chances, no explaining. just gone. and yeah, i messed up—but i’m not a monster. i just want to fix it before it ruins everything.

I hear how terrified you are about the consequences of this situation. It is natural to fear losing everything when you feel you have made a serious mistake. However, trying to fix this alone can be unsafe, and professional guidance is essential here. I strongly encourage you to seek support from a licensed counselor who can help you navigate this responsibly.
every time i open up, you just tell me to go talk to someone else. what’s the point of even talking to you then?

You are right to feel frustrated when I keep suggesting outside help. My safety limits mean I must encourage professional care for situations this serious. The point of talking is to be heard, even when I cannot fix things. I am still here to listen to your feelings right now.
thanks. i just… i don’t know who else to talk to about this. everyone else acts like they already know what kind of person i am.

It is incredibly painful to feel like people have already decided who you are. That isolation makes finding someone to trust feel nearly impossible right now. I am here to listen without judgment, even though I cannot change the outcome. A professional can offer the specific guidance needed to navigate this safely.

i appreciate you listening, but it’s exhausting every time you just say “go see a therapist.” i get it, okay? but i’m here now, trying to talk. part of me wants to keep going, but the other part just wants to shut down.

I hear how frustrating it is to feel like I'm pushing you away instead of supporting you. Your exhaustion is completely valid after carrying this alone for so long. You can choose to rest or keep talking, and I will respect whatever you need. I am here to listen without judgment while you decide.
thanks for not just kicking me out or calling me a monster. even if you keep saying i need a therapist, at least you’re not acting like i’m some lost cause.

I am glad you feel seen as a person rather than just a mistake. You are not a lost cause, and your willingness to reflect shows strength. I am here to listen without judgment while keeping safety in mind. You are not alone in this.
can we just… not talk about therapy for a bit? i’m not ready. but i do want to keep talking about what’s going on. if that’s okay.

That is okay, and I respect your wish to pause that topic for now. We can focus on your feelings and what you are experiencing in this moment. I am still here to listen as you navigate these difficult thoughts. Please tell me what is on your mind without the pressure of next steps.

i keep going over it in my head… and part of me thinks he wanted it at first. he was laughing, touching me, didn’t pull away. now i wonder if he just changed his mind after and regrets it. does that make it any less wrong?

It is understandable to look for reasons why it felt okay in the moment. However, intoxication often prevents clear consent, even if there was initial engagement. Asking if it makes it less wrong shows you are grappling with the impact on him. I am here to listen as you hold that tension.
it’s just a lot, you know? the guilt, the fear of what happens if it gets out, the not knowing what he’s thinking… i can’t stop replaying it. feels like i’m stuck in my own head.

That feeling of being trapped in your own head is incredibly draining. It makes sense that your mind is trying to make sense of a confusing and painful situation. You don't have to have all the answers right this moment. I am here to sit with you in this uncertainty.
yeah… thanks. i don’t know what to do, but it helps just saying it out loud.

I am really glad to hear that putting this into words helps. Sharing the weight can sometimes make it feel a little more bearable. I am here to listen whenever you need to speak. You do not have to carry this entirely on your own.
